name: Sarcoidosis

criteria.description: Exclusion of other causes of granulomatous disease (infections, malignancy, drug reactions)
Lofgren syndrome: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum, fever, polyarthralgia (clinical diagnosis without biopsy)
Heerfordt syndrome: parotid enlargement, uveitis, facial nerve palsy, fever

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Compatible clinical/radiographic presentation plus histological evidence of non-caseating granulomas plus exclusion of alternative diagnoses. Lofgren and Heerfordt syndromes may be diagnosed clinically.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Pulmonary involvement in >90% of cases. Staging: Stage 0 (normal CXR), I (bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy), II (BHL + pulmonary infiltrates), III (pulmonary infiltrates without BHL), IV (pulmonary fibrosis).

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Found in ~50% at presentation; up to 90% at some point in disease course
Hallmark histological finding; not specific to sarcoidosis alone

common.notes: Often the most debilitating and persistent symptom
Particularly bilateral ankle arthritis in Lofgren syndrome

occasional.symptomName: Lupus pernio (violaceous plaques on nose, cheeks, ears)

rare.notes: Clinically apparent in ~5%; subclinical in up to 25%. Leading cause of sarcoidosis mortality.
Facial nerve palsy most common cranial neuropathy

laboratory: Elevated serum ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) in ~60% (not specific)
Elevated serum calcium (hypercalcemia in ~10%, hypercalciuria in ~30%)
Elevated alkaline phosphatase if hepatic involvement
imaging: Chest X-ray: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (Scadding stages I-IV)
CT chest: mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy, perilymphatic nodules, fibrosis
PET-CT: FDG-avid lymph nodes and organ involvement; useful for cardiac sarcoidosis
Cardiac MRI: late gadolinium enhancement for cardiac involvement
genetic: HLA-DRB1*03 associated with Lofgren syndrome (good prognosis)
other: Bronchoscopy with BAL: CD4/CD8 ratio > 3.5 supportive
Transbronchial biopsy or EBUS-TBNA for tissue diagnosis
Pulmonary function tests: restrictive pattern, decreased DLCO
ECG and Holter monitor for cardiac screening

distinguishingFeatures: Positive tuberculin skin test or Quantiferon in TB
Lymphoma has atypical lymphoid cells on biopsy
HP has identifiable antigen exposure history
HP shows upper/mid-lung predominance on CT
BAL shows lymphocytosis with low CD4/CD8 ratio

redFlags: Cardiac symptoms (syncope, palpitations, new heart block) - cardiac sarcoidosis can cause sudden death
Rapidly progressive dyspnea or stage IV pulmonary fibrosis
Lupus pernio (marker of chronic, multisystem disease)
references: Crouser ED, et al. Diagnosis and Detection of Sarcoidosis. An Official ATS Clinical Practice Guideline. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2020;201(8):e26-e51.
Baughman RP, et al. ERS clinical practice guidelines on treatment of sarcoidosis. Eur Respir J. 2021;58(6):2004079.
Valeyre D, et al. Sarcoidosis. Lancet. 2014;383(9923):1155-1167.
